Rules summary Contents 1 The Goal 2 Setup 3 Game flow 4 Turn Sequence 4.1 Play one action token (optional) 4.2 Choose A) Swamp Rescue 4.3 Or B) Move one animal 4.4 Resolve conflicts 5 First Phase End 6 Second Phase Setup 7 End of Game 8 Action Tokens Summary The Goal Each player secretly supports 2 favorite animals (positive victory points) and opposes 1 disliked animal (negative victory points). Earn points by guiding your favorites to their goal and stopping your disliked one. . Setup Each player gets: 1 secret Card of un/favorite animals + 3 tokens ( Swamp , Banana Peel , Escape ). Board tiles are arranged: Farm → 8 Path tiles → Lair of Predators. 4 farm animals are placed on the Farm and 4 predators on the Lair. . Game flow The game consists of two main phases : In the First Phase, the farm animals try to reach the Lair of Predators, while predators try to reach the Farm. In the Second Phase, the movement is reversed. After the setup, the First Phase begins. . Turn Sequence Play one action token (optional) See Action Tokens Summary below. . Choose A) Swamp Rescue Remove a Swamp from a tile with at least one animal on it. Or B) Move one animal From a tile with no Swamp token on it. Farm animal - Basic move = 1 tile forward | Special move = Dodge past a continuous row of any animals. End the move either on a tile in the row with at least one other farm animal on it or on the first tile past the row. Predator - Basic move = 1 tile forward | Special move = Jump 2 tiles forward (skip the middle tile). . Resolve conflicts If farm animals meet predators on the same tile: 1 vs 1 - the farm wins only if another farm animal is on a tile directly behind, otherwise the predator wins. 1 vs many - the lone animal loses. The losing animal is removed → its token is put to the scoring track. Other players may now use an Escape token to save the animal from elimination. . First Phase End The First game phase ends when all animals are either eliminated or reach the opposite side. . Second Phase Setup 4 farm animals are placed on the Lair and 4 predators on the Farm. Already placed tokens stay on the tiles; used tokens are gone. Movement is reversed (farm animals go to the Farm, predators go to the Lair). . End of Game When all animals finish the Second Phase, scoring begins: Add points you've earned in both phases from favored animals . Subtract points you've earned in both phases from the disliked animal . The player with the most victory points wins. In case of a tie → the player with more unused tokens wins; if still tied, victory is shared. . Action Tokens Summary Banana Peel Swamp Escape Place it on a Path tile where there is no other token or animal. An animal landing here slides +1 tile; then discard the token. Place on a Path tile with no other token. Animals cannot move from this tile while the Swamp token is there. At the beginning of your turn: Return any one animal from any Path tile back to start. During the other player’s turn: Return the animal that is being eliminated back to start.

I never used a token even ones but I'm not planning on starting a new game on BGA to figure it out. But who knows maybe in the future...

[Rating: 7/10] Race game with slight deduction element. I am quite impressed how this game works, it is easy to understand, yet scoring and manipulation of animals is tactical enough to make this filler quite fun. I think if could be great kids and family game.

[Rating: 8/10] Played on BGA. Looks light at first, but there’s more going on than expected. Fast and surprisingly tense for such a simple ruleset.

[Rating: 9/10] The game is very pretty and cute, but at the same time it can be very challenging. For the fact that it was a prototype, what I played, the game was very well balanced and meaningful. When I played it with friends, we tried to predict and guess other people's next moves and rounds as much as possible, which sometimes caused quite strategically challenging moves, but at the same time it can be played very relaxed, depending on how competitive the group is. For me, a great game with relatively simple rules, which also has a strategic side, even though it doesn't seem like it at first glance.

[Rating: 9/10] I played as a prototype. In my opinion very light-hearted and fun as a chill party game. However, there are some balance issues - which, however, cannot be fixed with the current design - if a player is to eliminate a predator and protect 2 farm animals, they are quite unlikely to win the match.

[Rating: 10/10] Based on playing the prototype, I can recommend the game to anyone who wants to play a quick fun filler. The game is dynamic and full of strategic twists combined with simple gameplay elements and rules, which I was pleasantly surprised by. It also has the advantage of being compact, which makes it ideal for me when travelling as well.
